On the 27 NEXT lines this project has itself judged — 15 later recorded FALSE, 12 recorded to HOLD — the gate flags 0.133 of the false ones and 0.000 of the true ones, a gap of +0.1333. ⛔ This design's MDE at 80% power is 0.300, so a gap of that size IS NOT READABLE HERE and neither 'the gate works' nor 'the gate is inert' is supported. ⭐ WHAT IS SUPPORTED IS THE BOUND: with n=15 false and n=12 held, this corpus could not have detected criterion validity unless it were very large. ⭐⭐ BUT ONE NUMBER HERE IS RESOLVABLE AND IT IS THE USEFUL ONE: the Wilson 95% interval on sensitivity is [0.037, 0.379], so the gate catches AT MOST 38% of the NEXT lines this project later recorded FALSE — an upper bound, and it does not depend on the gap being readable. ⚠ The point estimate 0.133 is BELOW the corpus base rate 0.2772, so the registered directional FAILS, and across the three extractor specifications the gap runs -0.2000 to +0.1333 — SIGN-UNSTABLE, which is what an unreadable effect looks like. ⚠ R707's word-scramble result — that 76% of this gate's flagging survives destroying word order — remains the strongest evidence about it that exists. ⚠ AND THE LABELS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT OF ME: they are independent of the GATE, which is the confound this design controls and the only one. An external judge remains impossible here. ⚠ UNIT GAP: instrument unit is A NEXT PARAGRAPH, claim unit is THE GATE'S PREDICTIVE VALIDITY.
